correctness.rationale: On the coordinate torus, unit multiplication and inversion identify the scheme-theoretic hypersurface singularity with the Jacobian scheme of a quadratic cycle. For odd length its Hessian has determinant twice the positive edge product; for even length the cyclic bidiagonal determinant vanishes iff length is divisible by four and odd/even edge-weight products are equal. A nonzero maximal minor gives corank two, two parity-supported kernel generators with all supported coordinates nonzero yield a reduced punctured line, and splitting the quadratic form gives exact nondegenerate rank n-2 transverse analytic normal form. Exact SymPy examples replay successfully and are not substituted for the uniform proof.

value.rationale: This resolves the naturally exceptional case left by the published polygonal generic singularity criterion: for all admissible balanced polygons it determines the entire scheme on the dense torus and distinguishes a smooth reduced singular curve of uniform ordinary quadratic transverse type from nonreduced or higher degenerations. This has direct geometric meaning for the singular stratification of the universal-adjoint hypersurface, not merely a numerical inequality or an arbitrary finite slice.
